Acquisition and disposition activity materially affects depreciation and capital gains or losses, which combined, generally represent the majority of the difference between Net income available for common shareholders and FFO. As discussed in the definitions of non-GAAP financial measures found later in this release, MAA&#x2019;s definition of FFO is in accordance with the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts&#x2019;, or NAREIT&#x2019;s, definition, and Core FFO represents FFO as adjusted for items that are not considered part of MAA&#x2019;s core business operations. MAA believes that Core FFO is helpful in understanding operating performance in that Core FFO excludes not only depreciation expense of real estate assets and certain other non-routine items, but it also excludes certain items that by their nature are not comparable over periods and therefore tend to obscure actual operating performance.</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font></p>

     <td style="padding-top:0.01in;white-space:pre-wrap;padding-left:0in;vertical-align:bottom;padding-bottom:0in;padding-right:0.01in;text-align:left;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#160;</font></p></td>

     <td style="border-top:0.5pt solid #000000;padding-top:0.01in;white-space:pre-wrap;padding-left:0in;vertical-align:bottom;padding-bottom:0in;border-bottom:2.25pt double #000000;padding-right:0.01in;text-align:center;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:right;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">17,662,513</font></p></td>

  <div style="padding-top:0.5in;z-index:2;min-height:0.4in;position:relative;box-sizing:border-box;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;"><font style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">&#160;</font></p></div>

   <table style="border-spacing:0;table-layout:auto;width:100.0%;border-collapse:separate;">

    <tr style="height:12.25pt;background-color:#999999;word-break:break-word;white-space:pre-wrap;text-align:left;">
     <td style="padding-top:0in;padding-left:0.04in;vertical-align:bottom;padding-bottom:0in;padding-right:0.03in;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;" id="nongaapfinancialmeasures6"><font style="color:#ffffff;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES</font></p></td>
    </tr>
   </table><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">For purposes of calculations in this release, Adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Income Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization for real estate, or Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">, represents EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> further adjusted for items that are not considered part of MAA&#x2019;s core operations such as adjustments related to the fair value of the embedded derivative in the MAA Series I preferred shares, gain or loss on sale of non-depreciable assets, gain or loss on investments, casualty related charges and (recoveries), net, gain or loss on debt extinguishment and legal costs, settlements and (recoveries), net. As an owner and operator of real estate, MAA considers Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> to be an important measure of performance from core operations because Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> excludes various income and expense items that are not indicative of operating performance. MAA&#x2019;s computation of Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> may differ from the methodology utilized by other companies to calculate Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">. Adjusted EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> should not be considered as an alternative to Net income as an indicator of operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Core Adjusted Funds from Operations (Core AFFO)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Core AFFO is composed of Core FFO less recurring capital expenditures. Because net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is added back, Core AFFO, when used in this release, represents Core AFFO attributable to common shareholders and unitholders. Core AFFO should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders as an indicator of operating performance. As an owner and operator of real estate, MAA considers Core AFFO to be an important measure of performance from operations because Core AFFO measures the ability to control revenues, expenses and recurring capital expenditures.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Core Funds from Operations (Core FFO)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Core FFO represents FFO as adjusted for items that are not considered part of MAA&#x2019;s core business operations such as adjustments related to the fair value of the embedded derivative in the MAA Series I preferred shares; gain or loss on sale of non-depreciable assets; gain or loss on investments, net of tax; casualty related charges and (recoveries), net; gain or loss on debt extinguishment; legal costs, settlements and (recoveries), net, and mark-to-market debt adjustments. Because net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is added back, Core FFO, when used in this release, represents Core FFO attributable to common shareholders and unitholders. While MAA's definition of Core FFO may be similar to others in the industry, MAA&#x2019;s methodology for calculating Core FFO may differ from that utilized by other REITs and, accordingly, may not be comparable to such other REITs. Core FFO should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders as an indicator of operating performance. MAA believes that Core FFO is helpful in understanding its core operating performance between periods in that it removes certain items that by their nature are not comparable over periods and therefore tend to obscure actual operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">EBITDA</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">For purposes of calculations in this release, Earnings Before Interest, Income Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, or EBITDA, is composed of net income plus depreciation and amortization, interest expense, and income taxes. As an owner and operator of real estate, MAA considers EBITDA to be an important measure of performance from core operations because EBITDA excludes various expense items that are not indicative of operating performance. EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to Net income as an indicator of operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">For purposes of calculations in this release, Earnings Before Interest, Income Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization for real estate, or EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">, is composed of EBITDA further adjusted for the gain or loss on sale of depreciable assets, gain on consolidation of third-party development and adjustments to reflect MAA&#x2019;s share of EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re </font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">of an unconsolidated affiliate. As an owner and operator of real estate, MAA considers EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> to be an important measure of performance from core operations because EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> excludes various expense items that are not indicative of operating performance. While MAA&#x2019;s definition of EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> is in accordance with NAREIT&#x2019;s definition, it may differ from the methodology utilized by other companies to calculate EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">. EBITDA</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">re</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> should not be considered as an alternative to Net income as an indicator of operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Funds Available for Distribution (FAD)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">FAD is composed of Core FFO less total capital expenditures, excluding development spending, property acquisitions, capital expenditures relating to significant casualty losses that management expects to be reimbursed by insurance proceeds and corporate related capital expenditures. Because net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is added back, FAD, when used in this release, represents FAD attributable to common shareholders and unitholders. FAD should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders as an indicator of operating performance. As an owner and operator of real estate, MAA considers FAD to be an important measure of performance from core operations because FAD measures the ability to control revenues, expenses and capital expenditures.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Funds From Operations (FFO)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">FFO represents net income available for MAA common shareholders (calculated in accordance with GAAP) excluding gain or loss on disposition of operating properties, asset impairment and gain on consolidation of third-party development, plus depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, net income attributable to noncontrolling interests and adjustments for joint ventures. Because net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is added back, FFO, when used in this release, represents FFO attributable to common shareholders and unitholders. While MAA&#x2019;s definition of FFO is in accordance with NAREIT&#x2019;s definition, it may differ from the methodology for calculating FFO utilized by other companies and, accordingly, may not be comparable to such other companies. FFO should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders as an indicator of operating performance. MAA believes that FFO is helpful in understanding operating performance in that FFO excludes depreciation and amortization of real estate assets. MAA believes that GAAP historical cost depreciation of real estate assets is generally not correlated with changes in the value of those assets, whose value does not diminish predictably over time, as historical cost depreciation implies.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Gross Assets</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Gross Assets represents Total assets plus Accumulated depreciation and Accumulated depreciation for Assets held for sale. MAA believes that Gross Assets can be used as a helpful tool in evaluating its balance sheet positions. MAA believes that GAAP historical cost depreciation of real estate assets is generally not correlated with changes in the value of those assets, whose value does not diminish predictably over time, as historical cost depreciation implies.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Gross Real Estate Assets</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Gross Real Estate Assets represents Real estate assets, net plus Accumulated depreciation, Assets held for sale, net, Accumulated depreciation for Assets held for sale, Cash and cash equivalents and 1031(b) exchange proceeds included in Restricted cash. MAA believes that Gross Real Estate Assets can be used as a helpful tool in evaluating its balance sheet positions. MAA believes that GAAP historical cost depreciation of real estate assets is generally not correlated with changes in the value of those assets, whose value does not diminish predictably over time, as historical cost depreciation implies.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:1pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net Debt</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net Debt represents Unsecured notes payable, net and Secured notes payable, net less Cash and cash equivalents and 1031(b) exchange proceeds included in Restricted cash. MAA believes Net Debt is a helpful tool in evaluating its debt position.</font></p></div>
  <div style="z-index:2;flex-direction:column;display:flex;padding-bottom:0.5in;min-height:0.4in;justify-content:flex-end;position:relative;box-sizing:border-box;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:9pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:right;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">13</font></p></div>

     <td style="padding-top:0in;padding-left:0.04in;vertical-align:bottom;padding-bottom:0in;padding-right:0.03in;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#ffffff;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES (Continued)</font></p></td>
    </tr>
   </table><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net Operating Income (NOI)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Net Operating Income represents Rental and other property revenues less Total property operating expenses, excluding depreciation and amortization, for all properties held during the period, regardless of their status as held for sale. NOI should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders. MAA believes NOI is a helpful tool in evaluating operating performance because it measures the core operations of property performance by excluding corporate level expenses and other items not related to property operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Non-Same Store and Other NOI</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Non-Same Store and Other NOI represents Rental and other property revenues less Total property operating expenses, excluding depreciation and amortization, for all properties classified within the Non-Same Store and Other Portfolio during the period. Non-Same Store and Other NOI includes storm-related expenses related to severe weather events, including hurricanes and winter storms. Non-Same Store and Other NOI should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders. MAA believes Non-Same Store and Other NOI is a helpful tool in evaluating operating performance because it measures the core operations of property performance by excluding corporate level expenses and other items not related to property operating performance.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Same Store NOI</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:8pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Same Store NOI represents Rental and other property revenues less Total property operating expenses, excluding depreciation and amortization, for all properties classified within the Same Store Portfolio during the period. Same Store NOI excludes storm-related expenses related to severe weather events, including hurricanes and winter storms. Same Store NOI should not be considered as an alternative to Net income available for MAA common shareholders. MAA believes Same Store NOI is a helpful tool in evaluating operating performance because it measures the core operations of property performance by excluding corporate level expenses and other items not related to property operating performance.</font></p>
   <table style="border-spacing:0;table-layout:auto;width:100.0%;border-collapse:separate;">
    <tr style="visibility:collapse;">
     <td style="width:100%;box-sizing:content-box;"></td>
    </tr>
    <tr style="height:12.25pt;background-color:#999999;word-break:break-word;white-space:pre-wrap;text-align:left;">
     <td style="padding-top:0in;padding-left:0.04in;vertical-align:bottom;padding-bottom:0in;padding-right:0.03in;"><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;" id="otherkeydefinitions7"><font style="color:#ffffff;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">OTHER KEY DEFINITIONS</font></p></td>
    </tr>
   </table><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Average Effective Rent per Unit</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Average Effective Rent per Unit represents the average of gross rent amounts after the effect of leasing concessions for occupied units plus prevalent market rates asked for unoccupied units, divided by the total number of units. Leasing concessions represent discounts to the current market rate. MAA believes average effective rent is a helpful measurement in evaluating average pricing. It does not represent actual rental revenue collected per unit.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Average Physical Occupancy</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Average Physical Occupancy represents the average of the daily physical occupancy for an applicable period.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Development Communities</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Communities remain identified as development until certificates of occupancy are obtained for all units under development. Once all units are delivered and available for occupancy, the community moves into the Lease-up Communities portfolio.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective Blended Lease Rate Growth</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective Blended Lease Rate Growth represents the combined weighted average of Effective New Lease Rate Growth and Effective Renewal Lease Rate Growth from our Same Store Portfolio for the applicable period.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective New Lease Rate Growth</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective New Lease Rate Growth represents the growth in gross rent amounts after the effect of leasing concessions for new leases from our Same Store Portfolio that were effective during the applicable period as compared to the prior lease.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective Renewal Lease Rate Growth</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Effective Renewal Lease Rate Growth represents the growth in gross rent amounts after the effect of leasing concessions for renewal leases from our Same Store Portfolio that were effective during the applicable period as compared to the prior lease.</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">	</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Lease-up Communities</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">New acquisitions acquired during lease-up and newly developed communities remain in the Lease-up Communities portfolio until stabilized. Communities are considered stabilized when achieving 90% average physical occupancy for 90 days.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Non-Same Store and Other Portfolio</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.507%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.556%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Non-Same Store and Other Portfolio includes recently acquired communities, communities in development or lease-up, communities that have been disposed of or identified for disposition, communities that have experienced a significant casualty loss, stabilized communities that do not meet the requirements defined by the Same Store Portfolio, retail properties and commercial properties.</font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:5pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Resident Turnover</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Resident turnover represents resident move outs excluding transfers within the Same Store Portfolio as a percentage</font><font style="color:#ff0000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">of expiring leases on a trailing twelve month basis as of the end of the reported quarter.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">Same Store Portfolio (or Same Store)</font></p><p style="margin-left:2.533%;tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">MAA reviews its Same Store Portfolio at the beginning of each calendar year, or as significant transactions or events warrant. Communities are generally added into the Same Store Portfolio if they were owned and stabilized at the beginning of the previous year. Communities are considered stabilized when achieving 90% average physical occupancy for 90 days. Communities that have been approved by MAA&#x2019;s Board of Directors for disposition are excluded from the Same Store Portfolio. Communities that have experienced a significant casualty loss are also excluded from the Same Store Portfolio.</font></p><p style="tab-size:26.66px;font-size:8pt;margin-top:8pt;font-family:Arial;margin-bottom:0;margin-right:0.537%;text-align:left;"><font style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:8pt;font-family:Arial;font-kerning:none;min-width:fit-content;">CONTACT:  Investor Relations of MAA, 866-576-9689 (toll free), investor.relations@maac.com</font></p></div>
